messages.subject: Error when manually creating IOU and BM objects
messages.subject_clean: Error when manually creating IOU and BM objects
messages.body_plain:
I have been following Appendix S3 in Calabrese et al. (2016) to creat and plot variograms from IOU and BM objects (tau velocity taken from variogram.fit), but I get the following error(s):
> vg <- variogram(F61.1997, fast=FALSE)
> variogram.fit(vg)
> iou <- ctmm(tau=c(Inf, 3.5))
> bm <- ctmm(tau=Inf)
> summary(iou)
Error in summary.ctmm.single(object, level = level, level.UD = level.UD,  :
  trying to get slot "par" from an object of a basic class ("NULL") with no slots
> plot(vg, CTMM=iou, col.CTMM = "#1b9e77")
Error in unit.ctmm(CTMM[[i]], length = sqrt(SVF.scale), time = lag.scale) :
  trying to get slot "par" from an object of a basic class ("numeric") with no slots

However, the models do seem to be present, as evidenced by:
> IOU_F61.1997 <- ctmm.fit(F61.1997, iou)
> summary(IOU_F61.1997)
$CI
                       low           ML         high
tau velocity (seconds)   0 3.375706e-04     3.255743
speed (kilometers/day)   0 4.090274e+02 40169.375327

I have tried specifying the tau(velocity) units with %#%, but got the same error. It seems like I'm missing something simple. Any suggestions?
Thanks,
Roy

messages.subject: Re: Error when manually creating IOU and BM objects
messages.subject_clean: Error when manually creating IOU and BM objects
messages.body_plain:
Hi Roy,

ctmm() creates a prototype/guess of the model, which is not necessarily complete. In this case, iou and bm aren't specified enough for summary() or plot.variogram() to work. You can run them through ctmm.guess() and ctmm.fit() with the data to flesh out the remaining parameters, like you did with IOU_F61.1997. plot.variogram() should work with CTMM=IOU_F61.1997.

Here summary() and plot.variogram() are both failing because they are looking for diffusion rate information, which was never specified (sigma in variogram.fit).

Best,
Chris

messages.subject_clean: Error when manually creating IOU and BM objects
messages.body_plain:
Hi Roy,

My suspicion is that you can't compare them because the IOU likelihood contains dependence on a prior (which we derive from the limit of a large OUF model)... and that prior is probably doing something beyond standard likelihood analysis.

However, you could look at the sampling distribution of tau_velocity, which when zero makes IOU become BM.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Cannot coerce class "structure("telemetry", package = "ctmm")" to a data.frame
messages.subject_clean: Cannot coerce class "structure("telemetry", package = "ctmm")" to a data.frame
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

I'm starting to learn how to use ctmm in R to estimate occurrence distributions via kriging and have an strange problem I don't know how to fix. After I import one animal's location data as a telemetry object with as.telemetry(), then try to make a basic plot, I get the error below.

> wht11_tel <- as.telemetry(object = wht11_df, timeformat = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", timezone = "America/New_York",
                          projection = "+proj=utm +zone=16 +ellps=GRS80 +towgs84=0,0,0,0,0,0,0 +units=m +no_defs",
                          UERE = wht11_df$hdop)
Maximum speed of 0.411 m/s observed in unknown
Minimum sampling interval of 58 minutes in unknown
Warning message:
In as.telemetry.data.frame(object = wht11_df, timeformat = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",  :
  No MoveBank identification found. Assuming data corresponds to one indiviudal.
> plot(wht11_tel)
Error in as.data.frame.default(x[[i]], optional = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = stringsAsFactors) :
  cannot coerce class "structure("telemetry", package = "ctmm")" to a data.frame

I ignored the as.telemetry() warning message, since the data does indeed correspond to one individual. Anyways, what 's odd is that I successfully imported & plotted this animal's data just yesterday with the same code. Even the example provided in Calabrese et al.'s (2016) MEE paper is giving me the same error when it didn't before.

> data("buffalo")
> cilla <- buffalo[[1]]
> plot(cilla)
Error in as.data.frame.default(x[[i]], optional = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = stringsAsFactors) :
  cannot coerce class "structure("telemetry", package = "ctmm")" to a data.frame

I get the same error when I try to run variogram() on wht11_tel, so I can't go on with the rest of my analysis . I don't think I'm making any coding errors & the last person <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/ctmm-user/q9GbsDT1yL4> who reported this problem inexplicably had the issue resolve itself overnight, so any ideas what's going on?

Thanks in advance!
-Emily Dinh

Hi Chris,

I'm struggling to fit a good model to one individual animal's data. It seems that no matter what parameters I try, the fit looks bad and identical to each other. I've attached figures showing the fit with whatever parameters variogram.fit() gave me without moving the sliders (default) vs. when I played with the sliders (adjusted). Zoomed out is on the left, zoomed in on the right.

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-UBO3j0uAfqE/WrU5mEZa6-I/AAAAAAAAAAM/PYcfsLaNTWYKZB4a79UKLUoYFP19F1idwCLcBGAs/s1600/wht11_default_fit_check_zoomed_out.jpeg> <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-1P9kiGmx1Gk/WrU5phqtXsI/AAAAAAAAAAQ/VKISIh9om90RwzD2sSWxLiMgFPGPmPOowCLcBGAs/s1600/wht11_default_fit_check_zoomed_in.jpeg>

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-bH9Uy-6XfNc/WrU56FUtL2I/AAAAAAAAAAU/K09xfydYZAIRjw1GAnHCxyJl2b3cvdNNgCLcBGAs/s1600/wht11_adj_fit_check_zoomed_out.jpeg> <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-uIXi3u4b8cU/WrU5-LtmT2I/AAAAAAAAAAY/cc1zSJw5_LIVP8BH6zYaGN1_xjGBEnGXQCLcBGAs/s1600/wht11_adj_fit_check_zoomed_in.jpeg>

I see that this animal has an undulating semivariance pattern, especially at the shorter lags, so would changing GUESS$mean from stationary to non-stationary help?

Also, I was browsing the R package description & Variograms and Model Selection vignette and read about circular/elliptical covariances. I'm thinking changing GUESS$circle and/or GUESS$isotropic from FALSE to TRUE could help my model fit, but I don't understand what that would do. Can you please explain what circular/elliptical covariances are? In addition, what's GUESS$CPF?

Finally, please suggest anything else you think would help with my model fit. I've attached my data for this animal & code to this post for your reference.

Thank you,

-Emily

messages.body_plain:
It's possible some global variables saved in workspace overrides some functions in package.
You can try to locate the problem by loading different sections of workspace and check which caused the problem, and further divide that section until find the cause.

Or try to use more specific names for variables/function names. The common names/good names often were taken by package functions.

messages.subject: Re: Model fit - playing with GUESS attributes
messages.subject_clean: Model fit - playing with GUESS attributes
messages.body_plain:
Hi Emily,

The initial value of the guess only matters in as much as ctmm.fit() is able to find the maximum likelihood estimate with optim(). What you have is probably the right answer for that model.

A periodic mean from vignette("periodogram") will probably capture the daily oscillation, assuming that isn't a sampling artifact.
The hump at 1 month... you might try also adding in a lunar periodicity. I can't see if its periodic or stochastic from the variogram, though.
The isotropic argument is not going to help. isotropic=TRUE gives you VAR[x]=VAR[y] and COV[x,y]=0, while isotropic=FALSE relaxes this assumption. Its generally safe to leave that up to model selection.

For occurrence distributions, only the short-lag correspondence really matters, though, and it looks like you already have good fit a few lags out.

Best,
Chris

messages.body_plain:
No, but lunar harmonics can make arbitrary periodic shapes.

Keeping things as simple as possible, the variogram you see is a sum of deterministic (mean/trend) and stochastic (autocorrelation function) movement components and telemetry error. That kind of tweaking of the model needs to be done at the level of the model components.

>From what I can see of your variogram, it looks like there is a daily periodicity shifting around within monthly range (or monthly periodicity). Right now, only the latter is coded in the package, but the former will come within a year or so now that the Kalman filter code has been upgraded.

Best,
Chris

It's very common for TIFF files have the color reversed because the mishandling of various software. It could be either in R side or ArcMap side.

https://support.esri.com/en/technical-article/0000013

messages.body_plain:
Hi Emily,

That looks correct for the CDF. The CDF ranges from 0 at the innermost contour to 1 at the outermost contour. High CDF value does not mean high probability but high quantile value. E.g., the 95% contour is defined by CDF=0.95.

If you had exported the PDF or PMF, then it would have been as you expected.

Best,
Chris
